text:
Pierre Rehov, Gatestone Institute
Russian President Vladimir Putin has rediscovered the vocabulary of peace at the precise moment his army is taking Ukraine apart, one bridge and one power station at a time.

On September 25, addressing Russian journalists, he said that every proposal for settling the four-and-a-half-year war remained on the table, then attached the condition that empties the offer of content. "We are ready for talks and to wrap them up as soon as possible, but on conditions acceptable for the Russian people," Putin said. Moscow would first assess what served its own interests.

US President Donald J. Trump would do well to read that statement as a description of Putin's method. A leader preparing to end a war does not reserve for himself both the calendar of diplomacy and unrestricted freedom of fire. Putin, in a single appearance, claimed both, In doing so, he put negotiation where the Kremlin has always kept it, among the instruments of his war.

Washington was asked to hold its fire for the sake of diplomacy; then, in early October, Russia returned to bombing Kyiv's bridges six times in an apparent attempt to cut the capital city in two and sever its supply routes.

The error would be to read Putin's presence at the negotiating table as a decision to stop the war. In 1994, Russia signed the Budapest Memorandum, assuring Ukraine that if it gave up its nuclear weapons, Russia would not attack it. Ukraine, tragically, kept its part of the bargain.

Eight years of playing at process had cost Putin nothing and had given him time, which is what diplomacy without enforceable consequences reliably gives an aggressor.
A further development calls for serious caution. According to reporting published on October 3, the American-Russian discussions have widened to include a redolent multibillion-dollar sale of the international assets, refineries, oil fields and gas stations of Russia's Lukoil, which are currently under American sanctions. Putin raised the transaction himself at the Kremlin on September 5, in his meeting with US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, as proof that Russians could again do business with the United States!

So, commercial "normalization" was placed on the table during the same weeks as the bombardment intensified.... [F]or Moscow, prolonging talks is the perfect course, and a settlement can remain one meeting away indefinitely.

After Benedict Arnold met with a British major named John Andre to discuss what the Brits would offer in exchange for information, the fact of their meeting leaked and both men scurried to get away. 
 Arnold managed to make good his escape.  But Major Andre had originally intended to leave the area via the British warship HMS Vulture. and that ship had already been spotted and forced to withdraw under heavy shore battery fire. As an alternative, Arnold gave Andre some civilian clothes and a fake passport under the name "John Anderson."   Arnold also insisted that Andre hide the maps and other documents he'd given him in his boots.
 Andre's escape went horribly wrong when he met a trio of American militiamen, one of whom happened to be wearing a discarded Hessian coat, and he mistook them for loyalists. text:
Your Excellency Sir
@KagutaMuseveni
, thank you for opening up this timely Pan African debate for which I am passionate about.

“UNTIL AFRICA IS CONFRONTED WITH AN EXISTENTIAL THREAT EQUIVALENT TO COLONIALISM, AFRICAN UNITY REMAINS A DREAM, 
“UNTIL EVERY AFRICAN LEADER SEES AND TREATS IMPERIALIST OR AGENTS OF IMPERIALISM AS AN EMINENT DANGER, A LION ADVANCING TO ATTACK PREY, AFRICAN UNITY REMAINS A DREAM”
Sir, in your post, you argued the young people to rally behind the African economic integration and the African Political integration. Yes, this is what Africa needs; young or old, black or white, believers or non-believers, living in Africa or in the diaspora. 
The barbaric colonisation of Africa was facilitated by characters like King Leopold 11 who in 1883 wrote a letter to the missionaries in Africa to interpret the bible in a way that protected and promoted their interests. To indoctrinate young people so they don’t revolt, to offer total submission and obedience. The following biblical verses would be recited recited on a daily basis, Matthew 5:3 "Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven" Matthew 19:23–24: "Truly, I say to you, only with difficulty will a rich person enter the kingdom of heaven. Again, I tell you, it is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle than for a rich person to enter the kingdom of God." Luke 16:19-27 “The parable of the poor man and the rich man” Poor man died, went to heaven. Rich man died and went to hell. 

In 1835, another notable British figure, Lord Macaulay produced a reconnaissance report to British Parliament that paved way for European colonisation. He proposed the replacement of the ancient rich African civilisation (governance, trade, architecture, science etc), break the cultural backbone, devilise their strong religious beliefs, destroy their defence systems, halt their technological advancement by cutting off figures of those who were engaged in blacksmith etc. This was meant to mentally colonise them that everything foreign is better than their own, so they lose their self-esteem, their culture, develop self-hatred etc. This approach was applied in all British colonies. It took the British 50 years strategizing on how to subjugate us (1835 – 1885). Recently, the 81st UN General Assembly was held in New York, the Israel-Palestinian crisis took centre stage. Africa, our motherland, is engrossed in similar or worse crisis in over ten countries (Cabo Delgado-Mozambique, Eastern DRC, CAR, Somalia, Tigray-Ethiopia, Darfur-Sudan, Mali, Niger, Burkina Faso, Biafra-Nigeria, Ambazonia-Cameroon etc) but not a single African president mentioned about one, even in passing. Tragedy of Africa. ‘Eshongo nokweririra’.

In respect to the above, critical questions must come into our minds to properly comprehend where we are coming from, how we got there, where we are, where we need to be and what we need to do different to get there; Why was Africa colonized? Are they the same reasons for the current state of affairs? Why was Ethiopia able to escape colonialism? Is the Sahel states model a beacon of hope to be replicated? Who will be our voice at such UN fora if our leaders don’t? How do we adopt a democracy that suits Africa’s unique situation? What must we do different to achieve Kwame Nkrumah’s dream? Who are the Kwame Nkrumah’s of today in the 54 countries? Who can mobilise them to have one voice, to speak up unceasingly? What action do we need to take, not when, but now? 

Sir, as a revolutionary leader, our Jajja, our Ssaabalwanyi, our mentor, you were there during the independence struggles, you keenly followed the events, you got enraged by leaders who betrayed us at and post-independence and you therefore committed the rest of your life to undoing this mess by being at the forefront of these regional  liberation struggles like FRELIMO-Mozambique, fighting dictators like Idi Amin of Uganda, Mubutu Sese Seko Kuku Ngbengu wa za Banga of Congo, Jean-Bedel Bokassa of CAR, Omar Hassan Ahmad al-Bashir of Sudan etc. 

The uniqueness of the first, second and third generation freedom fighters was that; They dreamt in unanimity, They felt pain in unanimity, They spoke in unanimity, and They acted in unanimity. 

Permit me to use a historical perspective to draw the attention of Africans to understand why and when Pan Africanism agitation started, its proponents and why it was achieved after 60 years. 

As early as 1900, the first generation of anti-colonial freedom fighters of the African–American and Caribbean origin kickstarted the Pan African journey led by figures like; Slyvester Williams, W.E.D Du Bois, Marcus Mosiah Garvey, George Padmore, later joined by Pixley ka Isaka Seme, who together with John Langalibalele Dube, Sol Praatje founded South African Native National Congress (SANNC) in 1912 which metamorphosed into ANC in 1923, the oldest party in Africa. 

Then a second generation emerged in the 1940s; Kwame Nkrumah of Ghana, Sekou Toure of Guinea, Dr Nnamdi Azikiwe of Nigeria, Modibe Keita of Mali, Sylvanus Olympio of Togo, Amilcar Cabraal of Guinea Bissau, Gamel Abdu Nasser of Egypt, Ahmed Ben Bella of Algeria, Nelson Mandela of https://t.co/lXvpqi7BWE, Mwalimu Julius Nyerere Kambarage of Tanzania, Hastings Kamzo Banda of Malawi, Kenneth Kaunda of Zambia, Edwardo Dos Santos of Angola, Jomo Kinyatta of Kenya, Muammar Gadhafi of Libya, Samora Moises Machel of Mozambique, Robert Mugabe of Zimbabwe etc 

Then the third generation of the 1960s comprised of Yourself, John Garang De Mabior of South Sudan, Meles Zenawi of Ethiopia, Daniel Arap Moi of Kenya, Ali Hassan Mwinyi of Tanzania etc, to which you hold the present-day relay race baton. You are the hope of the young people, you are the hope of E.African political integration and ultimately the hope of African economic integration. 

Prominent Pan-Africanists who pushed for radical solutions to Africa’s problems were immediately eliminated; Kwame Nkrumah in 1957, in his independence speech, he said, “the independence of Ghana is meaningless if it’s not linked up with total liberation of Africa”. And in 1963, at the meeting of 32 independent heads of state in Addis had this to say “our goal is African Unity now…. we must unite now or perish. After three years, he was ousted. Patrice Emile Lumumba forcefully gave a fiery, defiant speech at Congolese independence in 1960 detailing the brutality of the Belgian rule, he was assassinated after six months together with his vice president Joseph Okito and a one minister, Maurice Mpolo. Capt Thomas Isidole Sankara in 1987, OAU summit in Addis Ababa pushed for a united front against debt, urging African states to collectively refuse external debt repayment. That it was our money coming back to us in ‘mwezunguruko’. He was assassinated after three months. Col Gadhafi Muamar advocated for the United States of Africa. In 2010, while in Senegal, he proposed forming a one million strong joint African military to protect the continents sovereignty and counter outsider powers like NATO. NATO assassinated him within one year. 

In short, Kwame Nkrumah spearheaded a United States Africa, his dream was buried by imperialists, Sankara resurrected it, same fate, Gadhafi resurrected it, same fate, President Traole of Burkina Faso has resurrected it by asking the French and their ECOWAS to go to hell, now, He is number one on the imperialist hit list. So far 30 attempted coups have been foiled. Paul’s letter to the Galatians; Gal:3:1 who bewitched us, Africans? He needs our immediate military protection Sir. 

Therefore, does the current situation in Africa qualify the philosophical question that ‘the greatest leaders are produced in time of intense crisis’, an alarming crisis that makes it extremely hard for people to work, eat or sleep? How then shall we realise an existential threat since Africa has surpassed this stage and is in the comfort of; 1. Too much food to eat and shelter (comfort zone). 2. Worshiping muzungu and anything foreign. 3. Disunited along ethnic, linguistic and pomposity lines. 4. Begging syndrome in form of Aid, Grants, Donations etc. 5. Greed, low self-esteem and need to retain presidential titles. 6. Branding liberators like President Traole dictators. etc 

We need to take bold and decisive actions like the Alliance of the Sahel States (advocate for; one army, common citizenship, a common market, one currency, one Central Bank, one foreign policy etc). We need to overhaul the tools they used and are still using to promote imperialism. This will definitely take a while and some of us may never be there to witness it. Besides a generational leader is that one who plants a tree with no hope of ever enjoying its fruits. Henceforth let's maintain the drive so the future generations can have it better than us. 

The 13 north American colonies under the stewardship of George Washington won their independence from Great Britain in 1776, they didn’t want to taste the presidential titles of their small states, focused at the bigger picture of an economically, politically and militarily emancipated United States of America. Mwalimu Julius Nyerere Kambarage shared same view. He was willing to delay the independence of Tanganyika so that Uganda and Kenya would celebrate a federated independence together. Obote and Kinyatta couldn’t listen. 

Your Excellency Sir, the African relay race baton has been changing hands from generation to generation. The generation of Pixley ka Isaka Seme and Emperor Haile Selassie handed over the baton to Kwame Nkrumah, who passed on the baton to Julius Nyerere Kambarage and Nelson Mandela’s generation. Sir, out of your foresight and frustration with the dictatorial regimes in Uganda, you opted to pursue your studies from Dar es Salaam which became the Africa’s ‘river Jordan’ Matthew 3:13 where Mwalimu Nyerere baptised many including yourself. You hold the baton; it's a huge responsibility on your shoulder to mentor a generation to handover the baton to, to keep the forefathers dream alive for a greater united Africa. 

We should build onto the unfolding events in the Sahel region to trigger the final assault against imperialism. Thinking and working in unanimity is what will deliver this historical mission. 

My plea Your Excellency, using Article 32 of the constitutive Act of African Union adopted on 11th July 2000 – Lome, Togo cause or propose; 
1. AU to gazette an African HEROS day to be celebrated in honour of the great revolutionary giants who sacrificed, shade their blood for us to breathe? Some include Kwame Nkrumah of Ghana removed in 1966, Modibe Keita of Mali removed in 1968, Haile Silassie of Ethiopia removed in 1974, Patrice Emile Lumumba of Congo assassinated in 1961, Sylvanus Olympio of Togo assassinated in 1963, Amilcar Cabral of Guniea Bissau assassinated in 1973, Samora Moises Machel of Mozambique assassinated in 1986, Capt Thomas Isidole Sankara of Burkina Faso assassinated in 1987, Col Muammar Gadhafi of Libya assassinated in 2011 etc. 
2. Editing of anti-Pan African clauses like Article 4 that suspends liberation regimes which acquire power ‘unconstitutionally’ and calls for non-interference by member states, to give special consideration to liberation struggles fighting imperialism that has kept us suffocated. 
3. Recognition of the Sahel States with a view to re-admit them into AU. African solutions to Africa’s issues. 
4. African standby force be deployed in the Sahel region to support this daring youthful president who has spat in the face of imperialists, presenting a new wave of African liberation leaders prioritising sovereignty and defiance of neo-colonialism over traditional democratic norms championed by the west. We need to avoid scenarios like what happen with Libya when NATO prevented African intervention which you referred to as zalawo “African presidents on African on an African mission on African soil were ordered by NATO to go back”. 
5. The four African regional compatible blocs of the South, East-Central, West and North by re-organising the existing formations like EAC, SADDC etc to absorb more member states with a view to politically federate. 6. Prevention of Afrophobia in the name on Xenophobia, killing the spirit of African-ness and ubuntu. 
7. Teaching of African languages and make foreign languages secondary to raise our self-esteem put Africa first? Mandarin in the next 50 years will take lead in global economic transactions. Nyerere used Swahili to unite over 120 tribes of Tanzania. 
8. African heads of state to discuss how to end the on-going conflicts beyond the Sahel States. Such intervention at the time of need automatically causes them to think beyond their small countries. 
9. Overhaul of the imperialist education system to decolonise our mindset, adopt a curriculum that instils softwares of critical thinking, innovation, invention, African history, African cultural heritage etc. our story continues to be told by others. Our story is written by others. We are defined by others. We must change course. We must find our true north. Time is now. We must write our own story by defining what was, what is and what will be, according to the African comprehension and expectations for the stronger future Africa for Africans. 
10. Creation of regional specialised manufacturing hubs to one, end comprador bourgeoise and two, avoid duplication of locally manufactured products that shrinks the internal markets and discourages mass production? For example, Uganda could be left to produce KIRA buses and sell to EAC and to the African markets, Transformers-Tanzania, Volkswagen cars -Rwanda, advanced military equipment-South Africa, Ships-Egypt etc. That way we create a consummative local market for locally produced goods rather than relying on foreign markets. Buy Africa, Build Africa (BABA) 
11. Pulling of resources for infrastructural development connecting major cities that will facilitate trade across borders (fast railway networks from Cairo to Cape town, Dakar to Addis Ababa and Dar es salaam to Luanda) Hydroelectricity power dams (R.Congo which can supply power to The entire Africa), in land road construction be prioritised (like Uganda is doing singlehandedly in Eastern DRC). 
12. Teaching and adoption of our local languages as ‘main’ to decolonise our mindset, promote trade, raise our self-esteem and enhance a sense of belonging? This will help in the removal of colonial labels of Africans such as Anglophones, Francophones and Lusophones that keeps us divided according to languages of our former colonialists or our neo-colonisers for that matter. We could target Swahili to be the main language by 2070. -Zulu widely spoken in southern Africa -Swahili (neutral) widely spoken in East and Central Africa -Hausa widely spoken in West Africa and -Arabic (neutral) widely spoken in North Africa In my opinion, the continued interference of imperialists in the political, economic and military affairs of innocent 54 nations constitutes an existential threat which we can escalate to ACT as unifying factor to develop a thick skin, thicker than that of a honey badger (Swahili-Nyegere, Luganda-Ntaulila, Runyankole-Ekijuguta) a small animal that repulses lions. Just like Africa's liberation was ignited by the Afro-Caribbean giants, now we equally have a strong ally over there, Prime Minister of Barbados H.E Mia Amor Mottley

, who gave a stunning speech at 81 United Nation General Assembly advocating for Africa’s recognition at all levels, restoration of trust and equal treatment before the UN. text:
#AI #ArtificialInteligence
America cannot win the global AI race if Americans are afraid to use AI https://t.co/oHoKVZiKi2

The leaders of Anthropic, Google, Meta, OpenAI, Nvidia and xAI recently joined President Trump at the White House to sign a voluntary accord on artificial intelligence. Its commitments are concrete: stronger internal controls, independent outside evaluation and board-level review.

The harder question, which remains to be seen, is whether it will earn the confidence of the people expected to live and work with these systems, who have been increasingly resistant to AI proliferation.

America cannot win the AI race if Americans are afraid to use AI.

AI ISN’T JUST A PROBLEM, IT’S A SOLUTION. SOME PEOPLE ARE ALREADY MAKING THE MOST OF IT

I often say that one of the biggest challenges we have to fear about AI is the fear of AI itself. That fear is becoming a national liability.

In a new EqualAI survey conducted by YouGov, 46% of Americans said they would be uncomfortable with a company using AI in a way that involves them or their data, regardless of safeguards. Yet 71% said a positive experience with an AI system would increase their confidence in it, and 63% said the same of a positive evaluation by independent scientists.

That 63% is an important window into mechanisms to trust — and offers a bridge to build it. People do not want assurances; they want verification.

AI will deliver for our economy, national security and competitiveness in the ways we are envisioning only if Americans actually use it. A nurse who does not trust an AI-enabled diagnostic tool will not rely on it. A manufacturer that cannot understand what its AI agents are doing will not deploy them at scale.

AI 'DOOMERS' RISK KNEECAPPING US VS CHINA, BUT EX-PENTAGON VET SAYS BOTH EXTREMES MISS THE MARK

That is why we need to be thoughtful when discussing "pause," because if it does not include capable competitors, such as Chinese companies, the technology continues to advance but elsewhere and without the guardrails we’d like to establish. The question we need to answer is: what will make Americans confident enough to adopt AI?

The debate is too often framed as more rules versus fewer rules. A more useful dialogue centers on how we can build the governance capacity to let AI scale.

The public is telling us we have work to do. A recent Reuters/Ipsos poll found that 73% of Americans believe AI companies have not done enough to prevent serious harm from their technology; 55% said they would support slowing AI development. The EqualAI polling points to what could change that equation: 63% want independent scientific review of AI systems, while 60% support third-party audits. Sixty-eight percent say it is essential to be able to correct wrong information, and 65% say the ability to appeal an AI-driven decision is essential.

When I testified before the House Select Committee, I heard strong, bipartisan interest in getting this right. My message was straightforward: American leadership on AI requires leadership in AI governance. Congress can use authorities it already has, including procurement, agency governance and consumer protection, as well as clarifying AI-specific protections, such as establishing definitions and protocols for AI incident reporting, as they’ve done for cyber incidents, and defining accountability for AI use cases with higher risk levels and making AI literacy a national competitiveness priority.

And companies don't need to wait for Washington. Every leadership team deploying AI should ensure they’ve taken these four steps:

First, make AI visible. You cannot govern what you cannot see. Organizations should know the who, what, where, when and how: where AI is deployed, what it can do and access, who owns it, when it will be tested and how unexpected outcomes will be addressed.

WHEN AI TESTS CAUSE DAMAGE, WE NEED STRONGER SAFEGUARDS AND REAL ACCOUNTABILITY

Second, establish independent evaluation. The institutional model is open to debate. The underlying questions are not: Who evaluates AI systems? Against what benchmarks? And what happens when a system fails?

Third, create a system to identify and handle significant AI incidents. Define incidents and ensure all responsible parties understand escalation pathways and reporting obligations. We also need the federal government to establish these.

Fourth, require accountability. Every organization should have a point person for deployments in certain risk categories. As AI becomes more agentic, systems can take actions rather than simply generate information. Responsible officers should ensure an agent only has the minimum access required.

Finally, ensure your workforce and families are AI literate. People do not need to become engineers. They need to understand what AI can and cannot do, when to question it and when human judgment must remain in charge.

We have navigated technological inflection points before. Cars did not become less innovative when we established licenses, traffic lights and global safety standards. Those institutions made mass adoption possible. AI will be no different. Governance accelerates trust and, as a result, adoption.

The answer is not to slow technological progress until we eliminate every risk. Nor is it to tell Americans to trust AI just because we want them to. As we accelerate AI development and capabilities, we need to match pace with the mechanisms that enable our capacity to govern it.

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

America's advantage has never been simply building powerful technologies. It is that we build along with the institutions and standards that allow powerful technologies to be trusted and adopted at scale. This moment asks us to do that again.

In a 2008 letter to the Irish Times, he wrote:

Israel-haters are fond of citing—and more often, mis-citing—my work in support of their arguments. Let me offer some corrections. . . . In defiance of the will of the international community, as embodied in the UN General Assembly Resolution of November 29th, 1947, [the Palestinians] launched hostilities against the Jewish community in Palestine in the hope of aborting the emergence of the Jewish state and perhaps destroying that community. But they lost; and one of the results was the displacement of 700,000 of them from their homes. . . . On the local level, in dozens of localities around Palestine, Arab leaders advised or ordered the evacuation of women and children or whole communities. . . .

Most of Palestine’s 700,000 “refugees” fled their homes because of the flail of war (and in the expectation that they would shortly return to their homes on the backs of victorious Arab invaders). 

The displacement of the 700,000 Arabs who became “refugees”—and I put the term in inverted commas, as two-thirds of them were displaced from one part of Palestine to another and not from their country (which is the usual definition of a refugee)—was not a “racist crime” . . . but the result of a national conflict and a war, with religious overtones, from the Muslim perspective, launched by the Arabs themselves.

Morris wrote in his book the refugee problem were “born of war, not by design.”

text:
India’s Fragile Hegemon: Majoritarianism as Self‑Sabotage

India’s Hindu majoritarian project under Narendra Modi is no different from Sri Lanka’s Buddhist majoritarianism: both are assaults on pluralism that hollow out the very foundations of state legitimacy. When a ruling elite defines national identity through exclusion, it does not consolidate power—it fractures society. Sri Lanka’s Sinhala‑Buddhist nationalism fueled decades of civil war and ethnic alienation. Modi’s Hindutva project risks the same trajectory, heightening tensions in Kashmir, Punjab, and among India’s 200 million Muslims.

The Ramachandran Guha's essay calls this India’s “feet of clay.” That metaphor is apt. Modi’s electoral dominance masks fragility. By eroding institutions—judiciary, media, parliamentary debate—India weakens the very mechanisms that sustain long‑term stability. A hegemon cannot stabilize its region if it cannot stabilize itself.  

For South Asia, this fragility is not abstract. Neighbors see India’s unreliability in crisis management, trade, and security guarantees. Pakistan views Modi’s sectarian politics as a direct threat to regional peace. Bangladesh, once tied to India through liberation solidarity, now questions whether Delhi can act as a unifying power when its own minorities are marginalized. Sri Lanka, Nepal, and the Maldives all hedge, turning to China or the U.S. when India’s promises ring hollow.

SAARC, already paralyzed by India‑Pakistan rivalry, becomes irrelevant under these conditions. India cannot lead a bloc when its neighbors distrust its intentions and doubt its capacity. The vacuum invites external powers. China, through Belt and Road, offers infrastructure and trade corridors. The U.S., seeking to balance China, finds willing partners among South Asian states wary of India’s unreliability. India’s claim to be the natural leader of South Asia collapses when its neighbors see it as a destabilizing force rather than a stabilizing hegemon.

Modi’s policy fragility is thus strategic fragility. A state consumed by majoritarian identity politics cannot project credible power abroad. India’s rise is undermined not by China or Pakistan but by its own internal contradictions. Just as Sri Lanka’s Buddhist nationalism led to decades of instability, India’s Hindu nationalism risks turning its “superpower” narrative into hollow rhetoric.  

The lesson is clear: pluralism is not a luxury—it is the foundation of legitimacy. Without it, India’s hegemon role in South Asia will remain symbolic, while real influence shifts to external actors who can deliver stability and integration. Modi’s India shines brightly in electoral victories, but beneath the surface, its feet of clay crack under the weight of exclusionary politics.

i will go line by line explaining my original post to you like you're 5 because i'm petty enough to do so

lefaa's original post was "i miss simple hero designs that flow well together like infernus instead of this power creep mess" the key words here being "simple hero designs" he calls the opposite of this "power creep"

i quote retweet, which means what i say is in the context of lefaa's tweet. i put "power creep" in quotations because what i say is in reference to his complaint about complex heroes which he calls power creep despite not actually being called power creep.

"game just comes out and they need simple designs" valve is pre alpha developing a game where every system is up in the air. their priorities are in the core game and the nuances of a complex and intricate hero. players having to try to navigate such a hero while also navigating such a complex game would yield more feedback about the character being too hard and too complex than about the core game.

text:
If you’re a founder looking to hire your creative / storytelling / branding person, here’s how you do it: 

First, understand why this is so hard: anyone who's genuinely good at content can probably make more $$$ working for themselves. Essentially, you're not just competing with other companies for this person, but also for this person's independence/freedom. 

If you're hiring from scratch (some advice):

Focus on up and coming creators. 

• Hire from 𝕏. This is where top writing/content talent lives

• Look for people already posting. Accounts with 1-30k followers are excellent candidates for Creative roles. 
Make a list of people you think can represent your brand well, and run outbound to these candidates (you can even have Grok Bot help you find good candidates here)

• Look for up-and-coming creators. Search for creators who are small but post interesting thoughts that align with your branding. Offer them to lead your brand.

Thoughts on how to incentivize talent:

• Get clear on what they want. Basically, what do you have to do to get this person to say yes? Think: What makes this opportunity a home run for them?

• Offer stable income via monthly retainer or salary (many people in content do not make stable income)

• Offer equity in the company if they become a key player

• Give them full creative control (let them cook)

• Equip them with a team. Don't make them be a one-man army. Give them the scope of your brand and ask them who they would need to bring in to support.

• Support their own brand: don’t make them choose between your brand and theirs. Give them kudos in public.

• Performance bonuses: reward people for good work. Don't treat content as a low-level role. It's not. It's difficult and requires skill to get right.

I've hired many people for these roles, and these are a few things I've learned.

text:
Sayyidunā al-Zubayr ibn al-ʿAwwām al-Qurashī al-Asadī رضي الله عنه was among the earliest Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, one of the ten promised Paradise (al-ʿAsharah al-Mubashsharah), and one of the most distinguished warriors of the first Islamic century.

He belonged to Banū Asad ibn ʿAbd al-ʿUzzā of Quraysh. His mother was Ṣafiyyah bint ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib رضي الله عنها, the paternal aunt of the Prophet ﷺ, making al-Zubayr his first cousin.

His father, al-ʿAwwām ibn Khuwaylid, was the brother of Sayyidah Khadījah bint Khuwaylid رضي الله عنها, the first wife of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, making al-Zubayr her nephew.

He was also the husband of Asmāʾ bint Abī Bakr رضي الله عنها and the father of ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zubayr and the distinguished scholar ʿUrwah ibn al-Zubayr.

Al-Zubayr accepted Islam at the young age of eight, according to one report, and was consequently subjected to severe persecution.

It is narrated that his paternal uncle would wrap him tightly in a mat, suspend him, and light a fire beneath him so that the smoke would suffocate him.

His uncle demanded that he abandon Islam, but al-Zubayr رضي الله عنه would respond:

“I will never return to disbelief.”

[Al-Ṭabarānī, al-Muʿjam al-Kabīr, 1/122]

His courage became apparent almost immediately after his conversion.

Al-Zubayr رضي الله عنه is remembered as the first person to unsheathe his sword for the sake of Allah.

It is reported that while resting in Makkah, he heard someone shouting that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had been killed.

He immediately rushed out with his sword drawn, prepared to confront those responsible.

The Prophet ﷺ encountered him and asked:

“What is the matter, O Zubayr?”

He replied:

“I heard that you had been killed.”

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ asked:

“What were you going to do?”

Al-Zubayr responded:

“By Allah, I was going to take revenge on all the people of Makkah.”

The Prophet ﷺ then supplicated for him.

[Faḍāʾil al-Ṣaḥābah, 2/914, ḥadīth 1260]

Thus, even before the establishment of the Muslim state in Madīnah, al-Zubayr had already demonstrated the courage and devotion that would characterize his military career.

When persecution intensified in Makkah, al-Zubayr migrated to Abyssinia with the early Muslims.

During their stay, a rival challenged al-Najāshī, the Christian king who had granted the Muslims protection.

The emigrants feared that his defeat would leave them vulnerable to persecution. They sought someone willing to cross the river, observe the battle, and return with news.

Although al-Zubayr was among the youngest of the emigrants, he immediately volunteered.

Umm Salamah رضي الله عنها narrated that the Muslims inflated a waterskin for him, which he placed beneath his chest before swimming across the river toward the battlefield.

The emigrants remained behind, supplicating that Allah grant al-Najāshī victory.

Eventually, al-Zubayr returned, waving his garment and announcing that al-Najāshī had prevailed.

[Musnad Aḥmad]

After returning to Makkah, al-Zubayr continued accompanying the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and subsequently migrated to Madīnah.

He never missed a single military campaign led by the Prophet ﷺ.

His reputation as a warrior became firmly established during the Battle of Badr.

On that day, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had two mounted warriors: al-Zubayr on the right flank and al-Miqdād ibn al-Aswad رضي الله عنه on the left.

Al-Zubayr wore a yellow turban.

It is narrated from ʿUrwah that Jibrīl عليه السلام descended wearing attire resembling that of al-Zubayr.

During the battle, al-Zubayr encountered ʿUbaydah ibn Saʿīd ibn al-ʿĀṣ, a heavily armored warrior whose body was entirely protected except for his eyes.

Al-Zubayr himself narrated:

“On the day of Badr, I met ʿUbaydah ibn Saʿīd ibn al-ʿĀṣ, who was so heavily armored that nothing could be seen except his eyes. He was known as Abū Dhāt al-Kursh.

He said, ‘I am Abū Dhāt al-Kursh.’

I charged at him and stabbed him in the eye. I placed my foot on him and pulled my spear out. I had to use great force to extract it because both ends were bent.”

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ subsequently asked for the spear, and al-Zubayr gave it to him.

[Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 3998]

This encounter demonstrated his remarkable precision, physical strength, and ability to overcome a heavily armored opponent.

The spear itself became a treasured possession.

After the death of the Prophet ﷺ, it passed through the hands of several of the Rightly Guided Caliphs before eventually returning to the family of al-Zubayr.

His bravery continued at the Battle of Uḥud.

When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ presented a sword to the Companions and asked who would take it and fulfill its responsibility, al-Zubayr was among those who volunteered.

The Prophet ﷺ ultimately entrusted it to Abū Dujānah al-Anṣārī رضي الله عنه, whose remarkable fighting al-Zubayr subsequently witnessed and described.

During Uḥud, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ also honored al-Zubayr with the words:

“May my father and mother be sacrificed for you.”

[Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī and Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim]

Following the battle, when the Muslims had suffered severe losses, the Prophet ﷺ called upon his Companions to pursue the retreating enemy and demonstrate that the Muslim army remained capable of fighting.

Al-Zubayr and Abū Bakr رضي الله عنهما were among those who responded.

Sayyidah ʿĀʾishah رضي الله عنها later identified both men as among those described by Allah:

الَّذِينَ اسْتَجَابُوا لِلَّهِ وَالرَّسُولِ مِن بَعْدِ مَا أَصَابَهُمُ الْقَرْحُ

“Those who responded to Allah and the Messenger after injury had struck them.”

[Qurʾān 3:172]

Al-Zubayr also witnessed the aftermath of the martyrdom of his maternal uncle, Sayyidunā Ḥamzah ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib رضي الله عنه.

When his mother, Ṣafiyyah رضي الله عنها, approached the battlefield to see her brother, al-Zubayr attempted to prevent her from witnessing his mutilated body, acting upon the instruction of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.

She nevertheless expressed patience and acceptance of Allah's decree.

She had brought two pieces of cloth for her brother's burial, but when the Muslims discovered another fallen Anṣārī who lacked a shroud, they divided the cloths between the two martyrs.

Al-Zubayr continued distinguishing himself during the subsequent campaigns.

At the Battle of the Trench, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sought information concerning Banū Qurayẓah.

He asked:

“Who will bring me news of Banū Qurayẓah?”

Al-Zubayr immediately volunteered.

The Prophet ﷺ repeated the request a second and third time, and on each occasion al-Zubayr offered to undertake the mission.

He rode into the territory of Banū Qurayẓah and returned with the necessary information.

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ then declared:

“Every Prophet has a disciple (ḥawārī), and my disciple is al-Zubayr.”

[Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 2414]

The title ḥawārī distinguished al-Zubayr as a particularly devoted helper and disciple of the Prophet ﷺ.

It was among the greatest honors conferred upon him.

Al-Zubayr continued serving the Messenger of Allah ﷺ until his passing, participating in the campaigns through which Islam became established throughout Arabia.

During the Conquest of Makkah in 8 AH, al-Zubayr رضي الله عنه was entrusted with carrying the standard of the Muhājirūn, the early Muslims who had migrated from Makkah to Madīnah.

The historical accounts also identify him as commander of the left wing of the Muslim army during the conquest.

However, his military career did not end with the Prophetic period.

Under the Rightly Guided Caliphs, al-Zubayr participated in the great conquests against the Byzantine Empire.

His courage became especially apparent at the Battle of Yarmūk.

On that day, several of the Companions encouraged him to charge against the Byzantine formations, promising that they would follow him.

Al-Zubayr replied:

“If I attack, you will abandon me.”

They assured him that they would not.

He charged directly into the Byzantine ranks, penetrating their formations and passing through them.

However, the other fighters failed to follow him. 

Al-Zubayr found himself alone among the enemy.

He turned and fought his way back toward the Muslim lines. As he returned, Byzantine soldiers seized his horse's reins and struck him twice on the shoulder.

Both wounds were inflicted near an older injury he had sustained at Badr.

His son ʿUrwah later recalled:

“When I was a child, I used to put my fingers into those scars while playing.”

[Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārīn 3975]

The narration also mentions that his son ʿAbd Allāh, then a young boy, accompanied him during the campaign and had been placed on horseback under another man's supervision.

Al-Dhahabī suggested that the encounter may instead have occurred at al-Yamāmah, based on the age mentioned for ʿAbd Allāh, although the narration in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī explicitly identifies Yarmūk.

In either case, the account preserves an extraordinary example of al-Zubayr's willingness to penetrate enemy formations even when unsupported.

His service continued beyond Syria.

During the caliphate of Sayyidunā ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb رضي الله عنه, al-Zubayr was dispatched to Egypt as part of the reinforcements sent to Sayyidunā ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ رضي الله عنه.

The Muslim army had encountered determined Byzantine resistance, particularly around the fortified stronghold of Babylon.

According to historical reports, ʿUmar sent four thousand men under distinguished commanders, among whom were al-Zubayr, al-Miqdād ibn al-Aswad, and ʿUbādah ibn al-Ṣāmit رضي الله عنهم.

The siege of Babylon proved difficult.

Its defenders were protected behind imposing fortifications, and the Muslim army struggled to force an entry.

It was then that al-Zubayr undertook one of the most dangerous actions attributed to him during the conquests.

According to the historical accounts, he volunteered to scale the fortress wall. A ladder was placed against the fortifications, and al-Zubayr ascended with his sword. Upon reaching the top, he proclaimed the takbīr.

The Muslims below responded and advanced toward the walls.

Other soldiers followed him into the fortress, and the assault contributed to breaking the Byzantine resistance.

The fortress eventually fell, opening the way for the further conquest of Egypt.

Thus, the same champion who had fought at Badr and Uḥud continued personally leading dangerous assaults decades later.

From the deserts of Arabia to the battlefields of Syria and the fortifications of Egypt, al-Zubayr remained among the distinguished warriors of the Muslim armies.

It's important to note that the virtues acquired throughout his life were not limited to just warfare.

He was also known for his generosity, concern for others, and devotion to Allah.

His wife, Asmāʾ bint Abī Bakr رضي الله عنها, narrated that when she married him, he possessed little wealth apart from a horse and a camel used for carrying water.

She would care for his horse, prepare its feed, and carry dates from land granted to him by the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.

On one occasion, the Prophet ﷺ encountered her carrying dates and offered her a ride. She declined out of shyness, remembering al-Zubayr's protective jealousy.

When she later informed her husband, he replied:

“By Allah, your carrying the dates was harder upon me than your riding with him.”

[Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī and Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim]

Despite beginning his married life with modest possessions, al-Zubayr eventually acquired substantial wealth.

He became known for his generosity toward the families of the Companions.

His son ʿUrwah narrated that seven Companions entrusted al-Zubayr with the guardianship of their children after their deaths.

Among them were ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf رضي الله عنهم.

Al-Zubayr protected the property of their children while providing for their needs from his own wealth.

He also demonstrated deep admiration for the martyrs of Islam. It is reported that he named several of his sons after Companions who had been martyred.

Among them were Ḥamzah, Jaʿfar, Muṣʿab, al-Mundhir, and ʿAbd Allāh.

He explained that he named his children after martyrs in the hope that they too would attain martyrdom.

Al-Zubayr was also careful to conceal his righteous deeds.

Among his reported sayings was:

“Whoever among you is able to conceal a righteous deed, let him do so.”

His standing among the Muslims was further demonstrated during the final days of Sayyidunā ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb رضي الله عنه.

When ʿUmar was fatally wounded in 23 AH, he appointed six senior Companions to determine his successor.

Al-Zubayr was among them, alongside ʿUthmān, ʿAlī, Ṭalḥah, Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ, and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf رضي الله عنهم.

All six were among the ten promised Paradise.

During the consultations, al-Zubayr relinquished his own claim in favor of Sayyidunā ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib رضي الله عنه.

The council eventually selected Sayyidunā ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān رضي الله عنه as the third Rightly Guided Caliph.

Al-Zubayr subsequently lived through the caliphate of ʿUthmān and the political turmoil that followed his assassination.

In 36 AH, he became involved in the events surrounding the Battle of the Camel.

However, before the confrontation reached its conclusion, al-Zubayr withdrew from the battlefield.

Historical reports differ over the precise circumstances of his withdrawal, but they relate that he departed rather than continue fighting.

It was during this withdrawal that he was pursued by ʿAmr ibn Jurmūz.

Al-Zubayr was killed near Baṣrah, with the most widely circulated account placing his murder at Wādī al-Sibāʿ while he was praying.

He was approximately sixty-four years old.

When news of his death reached Sayyidunā ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib رضي الله عنه, he condemned his killing.

It is reported that when ʿAlī saw al-Zubayr's sword, he said:

“How often this sword defended the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.”

Even in death, al-Zubayr's reputation as a defender of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ remained inseparable from his name.

One of the most remarkable accounts concerning his final days relates to his concern for fulfilling the rights of others.

Before his death, al-Zubayr instructed his son ʿAbd Allāh to settle his outstanding debts.

He told him that if he encountered difficulties, he should seek assistance from his Master.

ʿAbd Allāh asked:

“Who is your Master?”

Al-Zubayr replied:

“Allah.”

Following his father's death, ʿAbd Allāh carefully gathered his assets, sold properties, and repaid those to whom money was owed.

He continued announcing during the pilgrimage seasons that anyone possessing a claim against al-Zubayr should come forward.

Only after four years did he distribute the remaining inheritance.

[Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 3129]

Thus, even as he approached death, al-Zubayr remained concerned with the rights of others and the obligations he would leave behind.

Sayyidunā al-Zubayr ibn al-ʿAwwām رضي الله عنه spent his life serving Islam.

He embraced the religion while still young, endured persecution in Makkah, migrated to Abyssinia and Madīnah, and fought alongside the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in every one of his campaigns, then continued serving in the great conquests of Syria and Egypt.

His courage was recognized by the Muslims, his judgment was trusted by the Rightly Guided Caliphs, and his generosity extended to the families of his fellow Companions.

Above all these distinctions stands the testimony of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ himself:

“Every Prophet has a disciple, and my disciple is al-Zubayr.”

May Allah be pleased with Sayyidunā al-Zubayr ibn al-ʿAwwām, reward him for his companionship with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, his courage, generosity, conquests, and service to the Muslims, forgive his shortcomings, and gather us in his company in Jannah.

رضي الله عنه وأرضاه.

text:
Sarvapitri Amavasya (also known as Mahalaya Amavasya or Pitru Visarjini Amavasya) is the concluding and most significant day of Pitru Paksha (the 16-day period dedicated to paying homage to ancestors).
Key Significance
 * Universal Remembrance: While individual Shradh rituals are performed on the specific lunar death anniversary (tithi) of a family member, Sarvapitri Amavasya is meant for all ancestors.
 * For Unknown Dates: It is the designated day to offer prayers, Tarpan, and Pind Daan for ancestors whose exact death dates are forgotten, unknown, or missed during the year.
 * Karmic Healing & Blessings: Observing rituals on this day is believed to appease departed souls, help them attain ultimate peace (moksha), alleviate Pitru Dosh in the family horoscope, and invite prosperity and harmony.
Core Rituals
 * Tarpan: Offering water mixed with black sesame seeds, barley, and Kusha grass to the ancestors while reciting prayers.
 * Pind Daan: Offering balls made of cooked rice and barley flour.
 * Charity & Food Offerings: Preparing pure vegetarian (sattvik) food—often including dishes like kheer—and feeding Brahmins, the needy, and animals such as cows, crows, and dogs, which are considered messengers or forms connected to the ancestors.
Are you looking for specific puja timings, ritual procedures, or regional customs associated with Sarvapitri Amavasya?

Once the Roman government took over the Churches in Rome, (Peter didn’t create this and wasn’t your first Pope) it had to merge itself with pagan practices and beliefs in order to blend into Roman society without the masses rejecting it after hundreds of years of anti-Christian propaganda and the celebration of the killing of Christian’s. 

For centuries, Catholicism told the story of how it smashed paganism. The Roman Empire abandoned its idols, destroyed temples, and embraced the one true God. The truth? Catholicism  often dressed pagan gods up in new clothes, gave them Bible-friendly names, and put them back in the same spots they’d always been. In other words, it wasn’t a purge, it was a PR rebrand.

This isn’t wild conspiracy theory dude. Historians, archaeologists, and even some Catholic scholars will tell you the same thing. In order for the Roman government to spread its take over of Churches to the pagan masses of Rome, it had to absorb local customs and deities to make the religion more palatable to converts. People don’t like letting go of their old gods, festivals, and sacred sites. 

The Roman pagan government knew that. So instead of saying, “Your god is fake, burn his temple,” it often said, “This temple? Oh, it’s for Saint So-and-So now. Keep the temple, it’s fine”

They treated Saints exactly like the Roman pagans treated all of their different Gods. 

Examples…

Saint Barbara, the patron saint of miners.

Saint Hubertus, the patron saint of hunters and foresters.

Saint Leonhard, the protector of farmers and animals. 

Saint Nicholas, “venerated” as the patron saint of merchants and traders.

Brigid, the beloved Celtic goddess associated with fertility and healing, is perhaps the clearest example of the survival of an early goddess into Catholicism. Practitioners, mainly Ireland, pay tribute to Saint Brigid of Ireland who shares many of the early goddess’s attributes. Her feast day on the first of February falls around the same time as the pagan celebration of Imbolc.

We see the EXACT SAME thing at ancient pagan sites, where the gods and goddesses were believed to be in harmony with the landscape, embodying its qualities.

Ancient pagan beliefs survived into the Middle Ages.

This resulted through the centuries in Catholic saints replacing the old gods and goddesses.

It’s extremely clear to see former pagan gods and goddesses in Catholic saints and their attributes.

There are astonishing parallels between both belief systems, Roman paganism and aspects of Catholicism. 

The adoption of these pagan practices and symbols by the Catholic Church shows how the adoption of new institutions were difficult for pagan Romans and a blending of their pagan traditions was required for adoption of the masses after hundreds of years of the Roman government demonizing and slaughtering Christian’s. 

This all parallels the concept of diversity and multitude. In paganism, there were numerous gods and goddesses, each responsible for specific aspects of life or the world. In Catholicism, the “veneration” of saints offers a parallel system. Instead of many gods, there are hundreds of saints, each covering SPECIFIC attributes or domains. Similar to pagan gods, these saints can be both male and female.

• The Ultimate Tax Ledger: Priesthoods and temples—from ancient Sumer and Egypt down to the medieval Vatican—were historically the very first banks and money handlers. text:
How a Little Jewish Girl from Haifa Conquered Hollywood: The Story of Odeya Rush 🇮🇱❤️

Once upon a time, she was a little Jewish girl growing up in Haifa, surrounded by a large family, hearing both Hebrew and Russian at home, never imagining that one day she would share the screen with the legendary Meryl Streep.

Today, her name is well known in Hollywood. Her beauty is often compared to that of Mila Kunis, and she has become one of the successful Israeli actresses working in American cinema.

This is Odeya Rush, born Odeya Rushinek.

Odeya was born on May 12, 1997, in Haifa, Israel, into an Ashkenazi Jewish family. Her father, Shlomo Rushinek, comes from a family of Polish Jews, while her mother, Maia Greenfeld, immigrated to Israel from the Soviet Union. As a result, both Hebrew and Russian were spoken in their home.

Even her name carries a beautiful meaning. In Hebrew, “Odeya” means “I will thank God.”

She grew up in a lively household with six brothers. The actress later recalled with humor how protective they were, especially when boys came to visit. They would constantly enter her room offering food or drinks. She joked that sometimes it felt as though she had seven fathers instead of one.

When Odeya was nine years old, her family moved to the United States and settled in Alabama. She arrived knowing almost no English and had to adjust to a new country, a new school, and an entirely different environment.

The family later moved to Los Angeles, where Odeya decided she wanted to become an actress. Her parents were initially skeptical, but she was determined to pursue her dream.

Her career began with modeling and advertising campaigns for well-known brands, followed by small television roles.

Her major breakthrough came in 2014, when the young Israeli actress starred alongside Meryl Streep and Jeff Bridges in the science-fiction film The Giver.

A year later, she appeared opposite Jack Black in the popular film Goosebumps. In 2017, she played Jenna in Greta Gerwig’s acclaimed drama Lady Bird, which received five Academy Award nominations.

She later starred alongside Jennifer Aniston in Dumplin’. These roles helped establish her career in Hollywood and demonstrated that she had much more to offer than her striking appearance.

Despite building her career in America, Odeya maintained her connection to Israel.

In 2021, she appeared in the Israeli television series Ba’alat HaChalomot (The Dreamer), performing in Hebrew, the language she had spoken since childhood.

The year 2026 brought new opportunities to her career. She landed a major role in the crime thriller series Memory of a Killer, starring Patrick Dempsey, and also appeared in the Western The Isolate Thief alongside Sean Bean.

Today, Odeya Rush continues to work in American cinema, exploring different genres while maintaining ties to the country where she was born.

What makes her story especially remarkable is the journey she has taken: from a nine-year-old girl who arrived in America barely speaking English to an actress sharing the screen with some of Hollywood’s biggest stars.

Raised in an Israeli family with Polish and Soviet Jewish roots, she found her place in American cinema while preserving a connection to the language and culture of her childhood.

From Haifa to Hollywood — the story of a little Jewish girl who dared to dream and worked hard to make that dream come true. 🇮🇱❤️

Following the cybersecurity incidents I attributed to Meta and the U.S. Department of State in 2020, my primary objective was to settle down, establish long-term professional stability, and build a structured personal and family life. This was the rationale behind my request to transfer into Deloitte's Private Equity practice. 

However, subsequent cybersecurity incidents I attributed to Twitter during 2020–2021 further compromised my ability to pursue that stability, particularly given my concerns regarding Twitter's New York-centered social environment, including its artistic and drug-associated subcultures, political involvement, and broader media networks. I regarded these environments as inconsistent with my personal objectives, yet believed that unauthorized cybersecurity access had already exposed me to individuals and networks with whom I had never intended to associate. I had never originally intended to pursue entrepreneurship or independent investment management as an alternative to consulting; those decisions were reactive responses to cybersecurity concerns that I perceived as compromising the very professional institutions through which I sought stability. 

This included my concerns surrounding Accenture's decision in 2022 to assign me to Alphabet, an organization I associated with the reported 2020 incidents, followed by unsuccessful employment pursuits at PwC and Capital One and opportunities involving State Department-affiliated Afghan refugee projects, which represented a departure from my preferred private-sector career trajectory. When I joined Accenture in 2021, I had envisioned the position as a potential 10-year or even lifelong consulting career, not a temporary engagement preceding entrepreneurship. 

By 2023, having lost approximately 100 pounds, my priorities remained fundamentally personal rather than political: improving my health, developing meaningful relationships, preparing for family life, and establishing the structured lifestyle and professional continuity that I believed organizations such as PwC or Capital One could have offered. 

The subsequent pursuit of Skipyo and other entrepreneurial initiatives was therefore not the execution of a predetermined ambition to become a founder, but an attempt to recover professional autonomy after the conventional consulting career and personal stability I had originally sought became, in my assessment, increasingly difficult to sustain.

My hatred for White Men with MBAs, therefore comes from their provisioning of PWC, Capital One, and MBB styled organizations rather than any religious issues as I had viewed them as more grounded places for me than the Silicon Valley Tech Startup Culture, what the Top VCs were messaging about grand scale efforts, or State Department Conflict Embedded Juris Doctorate styled fronts or the eccentric Startup Founder behaviors or even Twitter's Political/Art Drug focus or Elon Musks daily media connectivity during that time. 

For myself I just wanted a role at Accenture for the longer term. The Skipyo 2022 investment of around 14k, had acquired 8000 shares in Rigetti Computing so by 2024 at Accenture, Skipyo would have been worth 300k, enough for Attorneys against Meta or X Corp or Microsoft for cyber breaches plus a down payment on a home. 

Instead their aggression combined with aggression from VCs looked to force growth.

text:
Here’s what it gave me:

**Anonymous Nobody** (X/Twitter: **@AFuckingNobody**) is a long-standing, pseudonymous NFT and crypto artist active since January 25, 2020. They describe themselves as an OG Crypto Artist/NFT Collector, visual artist, writer/poet, and creator of music and photos. Their self-description centers on being an “OG Satirical Trash Artist” and owner of the “Not-So-Supermarket,” with a blunt, politically incorrect, strong personality. Location references point to Southern California (U.S. signup). The real-world identity remains private by design—anonymity is a core part of the persona.

They maintain a central hub at the Linktree [https://t.co/5OtNgx34xt](https://t.co/LUuw9hH6wj), which aggregates OpenSea collections, music profiles (Spotify, YouTube, Apple Music), virtual land (Voxels parcels), and related sites such as https://t.co/Y5Q7oH9hFU / https://t.co/fxEfqTJn68. They also have presence on SuperRare, Foundation, KnownOrigin (legacy), Objkt (Tezos), and others. Follower count on X is in the ~14k range, with a very high volume of posts.

### Artistic Style and Themes

The work is rooted in **satirical trash art** and a deliberate “low-effort” aesthetic that is often high-effort in execution. Recurring motifs include consumerism, grocery/supermarket absurdity, glitch, experimental, photography, poetry, and critique of the NFT/crypto space itself. Collections frequently use irreverent, confrontational, or humorous titles (e.g., “Cheap Shit For Cheap People,” “Nobody’s Fucking Trash Art,” “ASCII Dicks,” “Me Flipping You Off,” “Fuck You Burger”). Music output includes early tokenized full-length tracks.

### Timeline and Notable Early Work

- **2020 onward**: Early activity on KnownOrigin, MakersPlace, Rarible, and OpenSea. One documented piece is “Shattered, but not broken” (KnownOrigin, created ~August 7, 2020; editions sold/gifted; featured in a 2021 CryptoHydrate Artist Collective video). Music includes the “The Mint Condition NFT EP” tokenized on MakersPlace in mid-June 2020 (full-length tracks as MP4s in limited editions—notable for the era when most audio NFTs were short clips). These early music works have been archived/gifted into collections such as Music Onchain.
- Prolific output across many years, with collections continuing into 2025 on Ethereum, Base, and other chains. Themes expanded into photography series, AI-related works (“The Artist & The AI”), experimental, and the dominant supermarket concept.

### Major Project: Not-So-Supermarket

This is the signature ongoing concept—a satirical grocery store of “low-quality” products, sale racks, ingredients, and absurd items minted as NFTs (often on OpenSea/Base). Collections include:

- Anonymous Nobody’s Not-So-Supermarket (multiple iterations, hundreds to thousands of items).
- Sale Rack versions.
- Related drops such as low-effort/trash art grocery dumps, eggs, and 1/1s.
- Supporting sites and tools (https://t.co/Y5Q7oH9hFU, https://t.co/fxEfqTJn68, ingredients-related, Voxels parcels for the store and an art gallery).

Items are often priced accessibly or framed ironically (lowball offers, damaged goods, satirical product names). The project blends visual art, performance/role-play as the store owner, and commentary on consumerism and the NFT market.

Other recurring or notable series include Creme de la Creme (2022), Mountain Life (2023), BASE 1/1s and editions (2024), photography collections, experimental/Async Art pieces, poetry/text works, and various legacy/vintage 2020–2021 collections. There are also personal collecting activities (e.g., an OpenSea gallery of collected works dating back to early 2020).

text:
1976. A garage in California. Two friends named Steve start a tiny company. They call it Apple.
Steve Wozniak designs the computer almost by himself. Everyone calls him Woz.
Steve Jobs sells it.
A handful of young helpers do the grunt work. Soldering boards. Testing circuits. Fixing bugs at the kitchen table.
One of them is Daniel Kottke. Jobs's close friend from college. The two had backpacked across India together.
He becomes Apple employee number 12.
The Apple II takes off. Families can have a computer at home for the first time.
December 1980. Apple goes public. Overnight, Jobs and Woz are multimillionaires.
But some of the garage crew get nothing. No stock. Not a single share.
Another early executive offers to match whatever Jobs gives Kottke.
Jobs says he will give him zero.
His friend from India. Zero.
Woz thinks that's wrong.
So he does something almost unheard of in Silicon Valley. People call it the Woz Plan.
He offers dozens of early employees up to 2,000 of his own shares each. Price: 5 dollars a share.
Up to 10 million dollars of his own Apple stock.
Kottke finally gets his shares.
Some of those workers walk away rich because of Woz.
Now do the math.
Apple stock has split again and again. By 2021, one of those 5 dollar shares had become 224 shares. Worth more than 40,000 dollars.
One share. 40,000 dollars.
A full block of 2,000 would have been worth around 80 million dollars.
Woz gave that chance away like it was nothing.
1981. Woz crashes a small plane he is piloting. He loses his memory for weeks.
It shakes him. He rethinks everything.
He goes back to Berkeley to finish his degree. Under a fake name. Rocky Raccoon Clark.
1985. He walks away from Apple.
And goes back to school. As a teacher.
He moves to Los Gatos, California. Walks into the local school district and basically adopts it.
The man who built Apple teaches fifth graders computer classes himself. For years. For free.
He buys computers and software for the kids and the teachers with his own money.
He wants kids to learn the way he did. Take it apart. Build it. Break it. Figure it out.
He bankrolls the Children's Discovery Museum of San Jose. The street outside is named Woz Way.
Jobs built one of the most valuable companies on Earth. He died in 2011 worth billions.
Woz handed out his shares and taught ten year olds.
He's in his 70s now. Still speaking to students around the world. Still telling them curiosity beats money.
Apple turned 50 this year. Worth trillions.
And the man who built its first computer by hand?
He's still on Apple's payroll. Since day one.
His paycheck is reportedly about 50 dollars a week.
