text:
SpaceX vs. $ASTS reminds me of Apple vs. Spotify.

At the time, Apple was already a tech giant with gigantic distribution, the iPhone, iTunes, and the App Store. And Spotify was a nobody, just a Swedish startup with a big vision and every incentive to make music streaming work.

You can imagine early backers asking: “What happens to our investment if Apple cuts you off the App Store?”

Never bet against Apple, right?

Then Apple launched Apple Music in 2015. A real thesis breaker. How the hell does a startup compete with that?

Had Spotify been publicly traded at that point, it’s easy to imagine early investors chickening out, turning into doomers overnight, and telling everyone it was going to zero.

But Spotify fought back. It accused Apple of blocking app updates and using App Store rules to disadvantage competing music services. In 2019, it filed an antitrust complaint with the European Commission and turned the dispute into a very public PR battle.

Through all of this, Spotify kept building, improving its product, and growing its subscriber base. Today, it has 300M paying subscribers and is the world’s largest music streaming subscription service.

Apple today is an even bigger giant than a decade before, and about 50x larger than Spotify. But in music streaming, Spotify won.

Yesterday, the market reacted as if SpaceX buying spectrum was a thesis killer for $ASTS. Add to that the fear that rocket companies could completely deprioritize launching AST’s satellites, and you can almost hear the same question: “How the hell do you compete with that?”

In fairness, depending on competitors, Blue Origin included, for launches is a real disadvantage. But Spotify also depended on infrastructure controlled by a giant competing directly against it, and that didn’t prevent it from winning.

I’m not saying AST will or won’t make it. It carries real risks and also offers a major opportunity, as many early-stage businesses have before it. How to weigh those two is up to each investor.

All I’m doing is rejecting the binary thinking that there can be only one winner in satellite connectivity, that you must own the rockets to build a constellation, and that the larger company must always win in every application layer it sets its sights on.

History shows it is a little more nuanced than that.

Zetwerk Looks to Clinch ₹27K Crore Valuation in IPO — ₹2,830 Crore Fresh Issue Plus ₹2,200 Crore OFS, 30+ Anchor Investors Lined Up, Weak Tech Sentiment Is the Key Risk

Core Theme 
Zetwerk is pressing ahead with a roughly ₹5,000 crore IPO at a ₹27,000 crore valuation, below its $4 billion private-round mark, backed by a marquee anchor lineup and 24% revenue growth, but a battered tech market means pricing and demand will decide whether the listing delivers on its industrial-growth pitch.

IPO Plan and Valuation
B2B manufacturing platform Zetwerk is preparing to tap the public markets, aiming to launch its IPO in the next few weeks at a valuation of about ₹27,000 crore ($3.1 billion), per two people with direct knowledge

IPO likely to comprise a fresh issue of ₹2,830 crore and an offer for sale (OFS) of ₹2,200 crore by existing investors

The company said it would announce the price band on Monday, October 12

Zetwerk is likely to file its red herring prospectus with SEBI within the next two weeks

Zetwerk did not immediately respond to Mint’s email seeking comment

Anchor Book
Over 30 foreign and domestic investors are considering participation in the anchor book, including Abu Dhabi Investment Authority (ADIA), Norway’s central bank, Goldman Sachs AMC, SBI and HDFC AMC

Other marquee names keen on the anchor book: SBI Pension Fund, BlackRock, Edelweiss Asset Management and Norges Bank

Source: “a diversified book that includes mutual funds and key FIIs”; more investors may be added to the anchor book by Sunday

Norges Bank and SBI Pension Fund said they had no comment; ADIA declined to comment

About Zetwerk
Founded in 2018 by Amrit Acharya, Srinath Ramakrishnan, Vishal Chaudhary, Ankit Fatehpuria and Rahul Sharma

Runs on its proprietary software platform, Zetwerk OS, which manages sourcing, production planning, supplier coordination and project execution

Operates through its own facilities and a network of third-party manufacturers, supplying products across utilities, renewable energy, consumer electronics, AI infrastructure, space and defence, oil and gas, industrial automation and aerospace, in India and overseas

Estimated operating revenue of ~₹15,900 crore in FY26, up 24%, per Inc42, citing a Crisil Ratings rationale

Has raised $931 million in 20 funding rounds as of September 27, per Tracxn; the last one, early this year, valued it at $4 billion

Backers include Greenoaks Capital, Khosla Ventures, Accel, Lightspeed Venture, Peak XV Partners, Avenir Growth Capital and Baillie Gifford

Market Sentiment Risk
The IPO comes when investor sentiment remains muted, especially toward tech stocks

Nifty IT index has fallen 24% so far in 2026, underperforming the benchmark Nifty 50, which has declined 14%

Weak sentiment could make investor demand and pricing key determinants of the IPO’s success, market participants said

Axis Direct (October report): IT services likely to report relatively moderate earnings growth in Q2FY27 as global demand remains cautious; ramp-ups in large deals, outcome-based engagements and rising AI-led spending should lend support, while margins are likely to stay mixed due to wage hikes, AI investments and deal ramp-up costs, partly offset by rupee depreciation and productivity gains

text:
This Jio IPO is set to be massive, aiming to raise ₹30,200 crore at the upper end of its price band. What's interesting is how they're pitching it, as a tech company, not just telecom. Akash and Isha Ambani have been taking this story global, meeting investors in the Americas, Europe, and Southeast Asia.

What really caught my eye is that existing big investors like Meta and Google aren't selling. Some are even looking to increase their stake. This is key to how IPOs work; when big players want in, it signals confidence and can influence how others see the issue. It also means the entire ₹30,000 crore will be fresh capital for Jio, with no offer-for-sale component.

The issue opens on October 21 and closes on October 23, with listing expected October 28. I'm always curious how the anchor book, which opens October 19, will be placed. That's where the institutional money is allocated first, often dictating the tone for the retail portion. If the anchor book is heavily subscribed, it generally means stronger demand for the rest of the issue. But it's also true that a ₹30,000 crore issue is huge, so even with strong anchor interest, getting the price right to leave "some value on the table" for retail investors, as , will be crucial for a good listing. I'm not sure I'd be jumping in on day one without seeing how this plays out.

text:
What if leverage was designed for HOLDERS, not just traders? 👀₿

I've been looking into @2FactorFinance, and one concept really caught my attention: Kelly-optimized leverage for buy-and-hold investors.

Most crypto investors understand the appeal of leverage. You get greater exposure to an asset without needing to put up the full amount of capital.

But there's a catch.

Leverage can amplify losses just as quickly as it amplifies gains. Financing costs eat into returns, volatility can erode performance over time, and liquidation can force you out of a position even if your long-term thesis hasn't changed.

So here's the question:

What if leverage were built for investors who want to hold through market cycles, rather than constantly manage short-term positions?

That's the problem 2factor Finance is trying to address. 👇

🧠 1. The idea behind 2factor Finance

2factor is building a leverage framework designed around long-term holding.

Its approach focuses on two major challenges:

🔹 Volatility drag: High volatility combined with excessive leverage can hurt long-term compounding.

🔹 Financing drag: Borrowing or maintaining leveraged exposure can carry ongoing costs that reduce returns.

The key idea is that getting the direction right isn't always enough. With traditional leveraged products, the path the market takes can also have a major impact on your final result.

2factor aims to reduce these inefficiencies through a system that separates Bitcoin's volatility into two different types of exposure.

🔵 2. BTC-Sr: The Senior side

BTC-Sr is designed to provide a more defensive, yield-bearing position.

Senior capital benefits from a buffer of Junior capital that absorbs losses first, subject to the protocol's structure and market conditions.

The yield mechanism is connected to the demand for leverage: when demand for the Junior side is relatively high, the Senior side can receive yield through the protocol's balancing mechanism.

This creates an interesting concept: investors seeking a more defensive exposure and investors seeking leveraged exposure can participate in different sides of the same system.

🟣 3. BTC-Jr: The Junior side

This is where things get interesting for Bitcoin bulls. 🐂

BTC-Jr is designed to provide capital-efficient, leveraged BTC exposure, with a current target of approximately 1.33x.

Why not simply aim for 2x or 3x?

Because more leverage isn't automatically better for long-term investors. The higher the leverage, the more sensitive the position becomes to volatility, losses, and financing costs.

2factor's approach focuses on moderate leverage and reducing the structural costs that can make traditional leveraged products difficult to hold over extended periods.

The target is about finding a more sustainable balance, not just chasing the biggest multiplier.

⚙️ 4. How does the system work?

One of the core concepts is called perpetual tranching.

Instead of treating all Bitcoin exposure the same way, the protocol separates it into Senior and Junior tranches with different risk and volatility profiles.

The system then uses rotation, rebalancing, and a bidirectional funding mechanism to help maintain the intended relationship between the two sides.

The BTC-Jr target also has a specific structural explanation:

• Approximately one-third of its collateral is allocated to fixed-term Junior tranches with roughly 2x BTC exposure.

• Approximately two-thirds is allocated to raw BTC exposure at 1x.

Together, that produces a target of approximately 1.33x:

(⅓ × 2.0x) + (⅔ × 1.0x) = 1.33x

I find this interesting because the target comes from how the collateral is structured, rather than simply selecting an aggressive leverage number.

🛡️ 5. What about a major Bitcoin crash?

This is an important distinction.

In the intended BTC-Jr structure, the leveraged Junior component can be exhausted during a severe drawdown, while the remaining raw BTC collateral continues to track Bitcoin.

That means leverage can compress toward 1x rather than the entire position being liquidated through conventional margin mechanics. Later rotations can gradually rebuild the leveraged component toward its target.

But let's be clear: this does NOT mean BTC-Jr cannot lose heavily.

Bitcoin can fall significantly, the Junior component can be depleted, and investors remain exposed to market, liquidity, smart-contract, and protocol risks. The Senior side also has risks and is not an unconditional guarantee of principal or yield.

Understanding the mechanics matters just as much as understanding the potential benefits.

📈 6. Why the Kelly-optimized approach matters

The Kelly framework studies how allocation, expected returns, and volatility interact to influence long-term compounded growth.

In simplified terms, it asks how much exposure may be productive without taking so much risk that volatility undermines the result.

The optimal amount depends on assumptions about an asset's expected return and volatility. It isn't a guarantee of future performance, and the theoretical optimum can change as those assumptions change.

That's why I think the broader philosophy is worth exploring:

Don't just ask how much leverage you can get. Ask how much leverage makes sense for the time horizon you actually have.

🌎 7. Bitcoin first. Then stocks.

Another interesting part of 2factor's vision is that its architecture is intended to be asset-agnostic.

Beyond Bitcoin, the same general concept could potentially extend to sufficiently liquid tokenized assets, including equities, commodities, and indices, provided the necessary market infrastructure and reliable price feeds are available.

If that vision develops successfully, the idea could reach beyond crypto traders and become relevant to a much wider range of long-term investors.

Of course, future expansion isn't guaranteed, and the design still needs to be evaluated on its actual implementation and performance.

🔥 My takeaway

The most interesting part of 2factor Finance isn't simply that it offers another way to get leveraged Bitcoin exposure.

It's the attempt to rethink leverage around three things:

✅ Capital efficiency
✅ Lower structural financing drag
✅ A design intended for longer holding periods
I'm interested in seeing how this approach develops, how it performs through different market conditions, and whether it can deliver on its goal of making leverage more practical for long-term investors.
Because in crypto, anyone can talk about upside during a bull run.

The real challenge is building a strategy that understands volatility, respects risk, and is designed for the long game. 🐂₿

Want to explore 2factor Finance yourself?

It is a matter of profound melancholy and deepest vexation to witness a profession, otherwise deemed noble, display so lamentable a destitution of knowledge regarding our sacred Constitution and those Fundamental Rights enshrined therein.
Be it known that under the majestic canopy of Article 19(1)(a) and Article 19(1)(b) of the Constitution of India, the citizenry is endowed with the inviolable liberty of free expression and the right to assemble peaceably and without arms. It is an established principle of our jurisprudence, affirmed by the apex court in the landmark precedent of Himat Lal K. Shah v. Commissioner of Police (1973), that the State may regulate, but cannot prohibit, the gathering of the public.
To demand a prior license or formal permission from executive authorities to manifest a peaceful grievance is a notion utterly repugnant to constitutional mandate. Mere intimation unto the authorities—offered as a courtesy of notice, not a plea for a crown concession—suffices the requirement of the law.
Let it be understood, with utmost clarity, that the mere donning of a black gown doth not an advocate make, if the mind beneath it remains utterly unacquainted with the very charter of liberty it is sworn to defend.

he had borrowed it from a criminal who was using the harbour to move stolen goods. when the police began investigating, he fled with his wife and baby to avoid being blamed for the operation. he had spent years working under a different name, too frightened to return. the waitress listened without interrupting, then explained the part he didn't know: her father had been the one who reported the boat missing, and the police had cleared the fisherman after discovering the criminal's operation. the family had never needed to disappear. the man stared at the old photograph and admitted that fear had turned one bad decision into thirty years of silence. he hadn't come to buy the restaurant out of nostalgia, either. he had learned that the building's new owner planned to replace it with luxury apartments, and he wanted to preserve the place where his daughter had eaten her first meal. the waitress checked the old ledger, found the unpaid bill, and tore out the page. “my father didn't keep this because he wanted the money,” she said. “he kept it because he wanted to know what happened to you.” the man offered to pay for the meal, but she refused. instead, she asked him to come back the following sunday and cook for the staff, just as he had promised her father all those years ago. he agreed. the restaurant sale was postponed while they negotiated a lease that would keep it open, and the man finally contacted his daughter, who lived in aarhus and had spent her adult life believing her father had died at sea. the old bill was settled that afternoon, not with money, but with the truth, a phone call, and a promise that this time, he would return when he said he would.

text:
The little girl from Full House was two different babies, and the show hid it from you in the credits.

Michelle Tanner was played by Mary-Kate and Ashley Olsen, but for years the credits read "Mary-Kate Ashley Olsen." One name. Producers didn't want audiences realizing the kid they loved was a tag team.

The reason is a law. California caps infants at 20 minutes of work per day on set. Hire one baby and your shooting day is basically over before lunch. Hire identical twins and you just doubled your footage for one character. That's why the Sprouse twins shared a role on Friends before Suite Life, and why half the baby roles you've ever watched were secretly two kids.

Which brings me to the two guys in this photo, Aaron and Shawn Ashmore. Their whole career started when a talent agent cast Aaron in a commercial as a kid, Aaron woke up sick on shoot day, and Shawn stepped in. That sick day was Shawn's first acting job. Early on, casting directors who couldn't tell them apart would flip a coin to decide who got a part.

It never stopped being tangled. Shawn appeared on Smallville in 2002 as a guy named Eric Summers. Four years later Aaron joined the same show as Jimmy Olsen. And Bryan Singer, who directed Shawn in X-Men, offered Aaron the Jimmy Olsen role in Superman Returns first.

So the Ashmores are the rare inversion of the whole playbook. Hollywood usually takes two twins and sells them to you as one person. These two spent 25 years building separate careers, and the audience merged them back into one anyway.

text:
Sir Eleak Forgedawn — Ever at Her Side

Eleak once dared to court General Charlotte Brunhausser. It ended spectacularly badly. Charlotte had little interest in romance; her devotion belonged to the art of war.

So Eleak chose another path. He became her student.

Her training was merciless, but he endured every trial. Charlotte rarely offered praise, yet the faintest nod from her was enough to drive him onward.

When the threat of the Valley arose, she gave him a single command as they rode into the mists:

“Stay close to me!”

And he always did.

Now a Half-Elf Death Knight stands beneath the tattered Brunhausser banner, his grey skin and spectral green eyes framed by long, dark hair. His ornate blade rests ready, his bow and quiver close at hand. Copper braziers cast flickering embers across the stone as the mists gather around him.

Whatever the Valley took from him, it never broke his final devotion.

Lord Rician Loyalar — The Roaring Ruin

Rician once led his tribe against Furyondy, trusting strength where strategy was needed. General Charlotte Brunhausser defeated his warriors with half their number, but spared the chieftain and offered him a new purpose: defending the Estate and its surrounding towns.

For years, Charlotte trained him personally. His strength grew until some claimed it rivaled the General’s own.

Then came the call to arms. Rician and his tribe rode into the mists—and the valley swallowed them whole.

Now a Half-Orc Death Knight stands amid the shattered canyon, green spectral fire trailing from his eyes. His colossal rune-inscribed axe rises in both hands, the faded Eye of Gruumsh barely visible upon his black breastplate. He roars at the grey fog, and for one brief moment, even the mists recoil.

Some warriors refuse to yield, even to death.

LONG NORMAN POWELL POST:

People are already talking about Norman Powell getting traded, or even him demanding a trade if the #ChicagoBulls aren't good?

I'm not sure why so many people in #BullsNation (or otherwise) think that the Bulls would prefer to move him during his first season as a Bull.

I believe all of those people are highly underestimating how important building the right culture is to Tiago Splitter and Bryson Graham, and that they're missing what I believe the Bulls sold Powell on when they signed him: building & molding something special.

The Bulls have TWO players on their team that are over 28 years old, including #NormanPowell. He's the Alpha Unc on this basketball team.

Having an All-Star veteran in your locker room who is your primary vocal leader (per Matas Buzelis on Media Day) and who knows how to establish/sustain a winning locker room (comes from Heat culture) is worth more than the people who keep talking trade are considering.

Do you guys really think Norman Powell signed his contract without understanding what he was getting himself into?

 I don't take Powell to be stupid. He knew the Bulls were extremely young and rebuilding. He knew they wanted to establish the culture, and he knows that takes time.

I'm 99.9% sure he knew that making the playoffs would be very tough, and that a play-in spot was more likely than anything in that regard.

In my opinion, the Bulls would need to receive a VERY rich offer in order to move Powell. I believe Bryson Graham sold Norman Powell on being a key piece to building something special, and that doesn't happen in half of a season.

And all of this is just about how important he is to the locker room - it doesn't even take into consideration how much his spacing is valuable for Matas Buzelis and Caleb Wilson. Teams have to take Powell seriously wherever he is on the court.

Put simply: Trading Norman Powell makes life for your developing young players harder - both on and off the court.

That doesn't sound like something I'd be interested in doing this season if I were the #Bulls.

Step into ancient Greece without leaving Tennessee at The Parthenon in Nashville’s Centennial Park. Originally built for Tennessee’s 1897 Centennial Exposition, the structure is a full-scale replica of the ancient Parthenon in Athens and was later rebuilt as a permanent landmark.

Inside, visitors can explore an art museum and stand beneath the enormous gilded statue of Athena, one of the tallest indoor statues in the Western world. Outside, the classical columns and surrounding park create one of Nashville’s most distinctive settings, especially at sunset.

Little-known fact: The Athena statue stands about 42 feet tall and was created to reflect what scholars believe the original statue inside the ancient Parthenon may have looked like.

Make it a stop on your next trip to Nashville. Whether you love architecture, art, history, or simply unusual places, The Parthenon offers an experience unlike anything else in the city.

text:
There is a group of Nigerians for whom complaining about Nigeria is no longer a reaction. It is a daily habit, a group identity, and in some cases a personality. Morning, afternoon, and night, the script is the same. Nigeria is finished. Nothing works. Nothing has ever worked. The past was a disaster. The present is a disaster. The future is already written as a disaster. They do not see anything good about the country, and they do not say anything good about it either.

If a story is bad, it travels. If it is false but sounds bad enough, it travels faster. If it is good, it is ignored, doubted, or dismissed as propaganda.
This is not patriotism. It is not even serious criticism. Serious criticism names a problem and points toward a remedy. What many people now practise is something else: a standing refusal to admit that anything in this country can be useful, improvable, or worth defending.

Yes, Nigeria has problems. Governance has failed in too many places. Corruption has cost the country more than it can easily count. Infrastructure is uneven. Insecurity has destroyed lives and livelihoods. Public institutions often underperform. Anyone who pretends otherwise is not being honest. But a country is not only its failures. A country is also its people, its markets, its schools, its farms, its traders, its professionals, its diaspora remittances, its culture, and the millions who wake up every day and still produce something.

Rather than ask what can be done, the conversation ends at the curse. Leaders are insulted. Fellow citizens are mocked. Anyone who points to a working business, a skilled young person, a functioning local initiative, or a sector that is growing is treated as naïve or compromised. Fake news is forwarded because it confirms the feeling. Bad news is shared because it keeps the group together.

Meanwhile, other people in the same country are getting richer, not because the system suddenly became perfect, but because they stopped waiting for the complaint to become a plan. They learned a skill the market would pay for. They studied past the certificate. They built clientele. They traded. They farmed with better methods. They wrote, coded, taught, repaired, designed, exported, or offered a service people actually needed. They did not deny the difficulty. They priced it in and moved.

Opportunity in Nigeria has never been evenly distributed, and it has never been easy. That is not the same thing as saying opportunity does not exist. It exists in trades that are short of competent people. It exists in professions where reputation still beats noise. It exists in agriculture, logistics, education, health, technology, construction, media, and small manufacturing, for those willing to learn the work instead of only learning the grievance. The person who acquires a real skill and uses it well will usually outpace the person who has mastered only the language of national despair.

Patriotism, properly understood, is not blindness. It is not singing while the house burns. It is the decision to treat the country as yours enough to improve it, rather than as a stranger you are only permitted to abuse. You can criticise policy and still refuse to traffic in lies. You can demand better leadership and still refuse to curse every neighbour who is trying.

Why is there never a sentence about what is working, what can be learned, or what you yourself are building? Why is every conversation a funeral and every forward a curse? Acquire the skill. Get the education that changes your capacity, not just your caption. 

Add value somewhere a buyer, a client, a student, a patient, or a community can feel it. Make an impact that survives the news cycle.
Nigeria will not be saved by a timeline of permanent pessimism. It will be moved, slowly and unevenly, by people who can see the cracks and still lay a brick. Complaining has had its turn. It has not built the road, trained the child, or paid the bills. Something else has to.

K&D DAILY DEVOTIONAL

Saturday, October 10, 2026

BEGINNING WITH GOD — PART 9

REST WITH GOD—NOT AWAY FROM GOD

Anchor Scripture:
“He maketh me to lie down in green pastures: He leadeth me beside the still waters. He restoreth my soul.” — Psalm 23:2–3

The weekend often brings a desire to pause, sleep longer, reduce responsibilities, enjoy family, and recover from the demands of the week. Rest is not sinful. Our bodies and minds have limits, and Scripture does not glorify exhaustion.

But there is a difference between resting with GOD and attempting to rest away from GOD.

David described the Lord as the Shepherd who led him beside still waters and restored his soul. The restoration did not occur through separation from the Shepherd. David rested because the Shepherd was present, leading, protecting, and providing.

True rest is not merely the absence of activity. It is the restoration of strength, clarity, order, and spiritual sensitivity in the presence of GOD.

A person may sleep for many hours and still wake emotionally burdened. Another may spend the entire day watching television or scrolling through social media and remain mentally exhausted. The body may have stopped working while the mind continues absorbing noise.

Entertainment can occupy time without restoring the soul.

Some people use the weekend to escape from everything that troubles them. But temporary escape is not the same as restoration. What is avoided eventually returns, and what is buried without healing may quietly become heavier.

GOD does not merely want you to stop. He wants to restore you.

Biblical rest includes trusting GOD with what remains unfinished. It means admitting that you are human and that the world will continue moving while you pause. It means refusing to carry responsibilities that belong to GOD alone.

Rest also exposes misplaced identity. If you feel worthless whenever you are not producing, achieving, serving, or solving problems, you may have connected your value to performance rather than to GOD.

You are not valuable only when you are useful to people.

Jesus invited the weary and burdened to come to Him. He did not simply command them to take a break; He offered rest for their souls. The deepest exhaustion cannot always be cured by sleep, because some weariness comes from guilt, fear, grief, disappointment, striving, and carrying burdens without surrender.

As you rest this weekend, remain close to the Shepherd. Let Him examine what exhausted you. Allow His Word to quiet your thoughts. Give Him the matters 

Do not merely escape the week. Let GOD restore you for what lies ahead.

SIGNS THAT REST MAY HAVE BECOME ESCAPE

- You continually avoid necessary conversations or responsibilities.
- Entertainment leaves you more distracted than refreshed.
- You neglect prayer and Scripture whenever your schedule becomes relaxed.
- You feel anxious or guilty when you are not being productive.
- You use sleep, food, shopping, or social media to suppress unresolved pain.
- You return from rest without renewed strength, clarity, or peace.

PRACTICAL RESPONSE

1. Thank GOD for carrying you through the week.
2. Identify what has physically, emotionally, or spiritually exhausted you.
3. Surrender unfinished responsibilities to GOD without abandoning your duties.
4. Reduce unnecessary digital noise for part of the day.
5. Receive appropriate sleep, nourishment, and quietness.
6. Spend unhurried time reading Scripture and speaking honestly with GOD.
7. Enjoy healthy fellowship with family and other believers.
8. Prepare peacefully for the coming week without allowing tomorrow’s concerns to consume today.

PRAYER

Heavenly Father, thank You for being the Shepherd of my soul. I surrender every burden, disappointment, unfinished responsibility, and anxious thought to You. Deliver me from false rest, unhealthy escape, and the pressure to prove my worth through constant activity. Restore my body, renew my mind, heal my emotions, and revive my spirit.

text:
MY 2 CENTS — OCTOBER 10, 2025: THE DAY $19 BILLION IN LEVERAGED CRYPTO POSITIONS WERE LIQUIDATED

Exactly one year ago, the cryptocurrency market experienced the largest reported liquidation event in its history, with approximately $19.1 billion in leveraged positions forcibly closed within 24 hours and around 1.6 million trading accounts affected.
Looking back at that day, I believe the most important lesson is not how quickly Bitcoin collapsed, but how a geopolitical shock exposed the structural fragility of a market increasingly dominated by leverage, automated liquidations and fragmented liquidity.

1️⃣ THE DAY THAT EXPOSED THE MARKET'S HIDDEN FRAGILITY
On October 10, 2025, Bitcoin was trading close to historical highs, supported by institutional participation, speculative positioning and expectations of further appreciation. Within hours, however, BTC had fallen more than 14% from its Friday high, while Ethereum and several major altcoins suffered even more severe losses. The scale of the event was extraordinary, but the underlying mechanism was familiar: markets had accumulated considerably more risk than they could absorb once sentiment abruptly reversed.

2️⃣ THE TRIGGER WAS GEOPOLITICAL, BUT THE CRASH WAS STRUCTURAL
The immediate catalyst came from Washington, when President Trump threatened additional 100% tariffs on Chinese imports, reigniting fears of a major escalation in the trade confrontation between the world's two largest economies. Global equity markets reacted negatively, but cryptocurrencies experienced a much more violent adjustment because speculative positioning and leverage had already created highly vulnerable conditions. The announcement triggered the initial repricing; the structure of the crypto derivatives market transformed it into an unprecedented liquidation cascade.

3️⃣ LEVERAGE TURNED A MARKET CORRECTION INTO A CHAIN REACTION
When traders operate with borrowed capital, adverse price movements can quickly erode the collateral supporting their positions. Once maintenance-margin requirements are breached, exchanges automatically liquidate positions to contain their own exposure. Those forced sales push market prices lower, reducing the collateral value of other positions and triggering further liquidations. On October 10, this mechanism became self-reinforcing across multiple trading venues, demonstrating how a market can experience extraordinary losses in positioning without any corresponding deterioration in the underlying technology of Bitcoin, Ethereum or Solana.

4️⃣ LIQUIDITY DISAPPEARED PRECISELY WHEN IT WAS MOST NEEDED
One of the most revealing aspects of the crash was the sudden deterioration in order-book depth. Market makers reduced exposure as volatility accelerated, while automated risk-management systems withdrew liquidity from already stressed markets. Under normal conditions, substantial buying and selling activity can be absorbed within relatively narrow price ranges. During a liquidity vacuum, however, even comparatively modest sell orders can produce extreme price movements. This explains why some altcoins experienced intraday declines exceeding 50%, while certain tokens briefly traded at extraordinary discounts on individual exchanges.

5️⃣ THE $19.1 BILLION FIGURE MUST BE UNDERSTOOD CORRECTLY
The frequently quoted liquidation figure represents the reported notional value of leveraged positions closed by exchanges, rather than $19.1 billion in cryptocurrencies stolen, permanently destroyed or directly removed from market capitalisation. The distinction is essential because derivatives allow traders to control exposure considerably larger than the capital deposited as collateral. Nevertheless, the economic consequences were very real: traders lost margin, forced selling distorted prices, market makers suffered severe stress and confidence in execution quality deteriorated. Moreover, because liquidation statistics depend on exchange reporting, the precise total remains subject to uncertainty.

6️⃣ THE CRISIS ALSO EXPOSED WEAKNESSES INSIDE EXCHANGES
The most controversial developments involved collateral valuation and temporary price dislocations on individual platforms. On Binance, USDe briefly traded around $0.65, while wrapped and liquid-staking assets experienced substantial deviations from their reference values. These movements affected positions using such instruments as collateral and raised serious questions about exchange-specific pricing mechanisms, oracle design and risk controls. Binance subsequently acknowledged platform-specific problems while disputing claims that they caused the wider crash. The broader lesson is that exchange infrastructure and collateral architecture can amplify market instability, even when the initial shock originates elsewhere.

7️⃣ THE DAMAGE EXTENDED WELL BEYOND LONG POSITIONS
The liquidation cascade also revealed that apparently sophisticated trading strategies are not necessarily immune to market infrastructure failures. On Hyperliquid, auto-deleveraging mechanisms resulted in some profitable short positions being forcibly reduced or closed as the system managed extreme counterparty risk. This matters because traders often assume that correct directional positioning guarantees a profitable outcome. In stressed derivatives markets, execution, collateral rules, liquidity availability and the behaviour of the trading venue can become just as important as predicting the market's direction. A correct forecast is not sufficient protection against an unstable trading environment.

8️⃣ ONE YEAR LATER, HAS THE INDUSTRY REALLY LEARNED THE LESSON?
The sector has continued evolving through institutional integration, stablecoin development, tokenisation and improvements in certain trading infrastructures. Some venues have revised collateral and liquidation mechanisms, while greater onchain transparency offers opportunities to examine market behaviour more directly. Nevertheless, the essential vulnerabilities have not disappeared. Leverage can still become excessive, liquidity remains fragmented and automated liquidation engines can continue reinforcing sudden market movements. The October 2025 event also demonstrated how closely crypto markets respond to global liquidity, geopolitical developments and traditional risk appetite, challenging the idea that digital assets operate independently of the wider financial system.

9️⃣ THE DIFFERENCE BETWEEN INVESTING AND SPECULATING BECOMES CLEAR DURING A CRISIS
My approach separates long-term accumulation from active trading. I continue to regard Bitcoin, Ethereum and Solana as assets worth analysing within a disciplined DCA framework, while recognising that each carries a different technological, financial and volatility profile. Trading capital, however, requires a separate methodology, predefined position sizing, controlled leverage and clearly established invalidation levels. The principles discussed in trading-discipline literature remain relevant: preserving capital and remaining operational after a losing trade matter more than attempting to capture every price movement. A strategy that only works while markets are rising is not a robust strategy.

🔟 MY 2 CENTS — THE MOST IMPORTANT LESSON OF OCTOBER 10
What happened one year ago should remain part of every serious crypto investor's understanding of market risk. Bitcoin did not suddenly lose its monetary properties, Ethereum did not cease functioning as programmable infrastructure, and Solana's long-term technological prospects were not determined by a few hours of forced selling. What failed was the assumption that increasing exposure through leverage could continue indefinitely without encountering the limits of available liquidity.

There is also a distinction I consider essential when discussing future crashes. A sharp correction driven by forced liquidations can create opportunities for investors with sufficient liquidity, an appropriate time horizon and a coherent accumulation strategy. But not every collapse is automatically an opportunity, and buying simply because prices have fallen can become another emotional decision when the underlying risks have not been understood.
I do not consider the objective of investing to be purchasing the absolute bottom or selling the absolute top. The objective is to build and maintain a strategy that remains financially sustainable through different market regimes, including those in which prices, liquidity and sentiment deteriorate simultaneously.

The real danger is often not the correction itself, but the combination of excessive leverage, inadequate preparation and the conviction that the market cannot move far enough to invalidate our expectations.
October 10, 2025, demonstrated how quickly that conviction can disappear.
One year later, the market may have evolved, but the fundamental responsibility of every investor remains unchanged: understand the instrument, control exposure, protect liquidity and never confuse surviving a market cycle with correctly predicting every movement within it.
For me, that is the real meaning of discipline in crypto investing, and it is a lesson considerably more valuable than any attempt to predict the next liquidation event.

Madison Act No. 4 — A Discussion on Practical Implementation in Washington State

A Proposed Seattle Pilot | 150 Words

Seattle’s experience with participatory budgeting offers a starting point for extending James Madison’s constitutional logic: bringing public decisions closer to citizens while protecting representative government and citizens’ petition rights.

We propose discussing a voluntary, legally authorized pilot in Seattle and a comparable Washington city. Both would convene randomly selected citizens to review a limited set of municipal budget proposals.

One would receive AI-assisted, source-linked briefings; the other would use human-prepared materials. Each briefing would explain the proposal’s purpose, cost, funding source, measurable benefits, risks, and uncertainties.

Citizens—not AI—would deliberate and decide within the authority granted by law.

After three months, independent reviewers would compare understanding, participation, decision time, transparency, and initial outcomes.

Both cities would share the findings and adopt whichever practices proved useful, subject to public consent and legal safeguards.

This is not enacted legislation, but a small, reversible experiment in making democratic participation more informed, fair, and effective.

Ms Suhasini Haidar @suhasinih, what if the most consequential question in your latest Worldview is not whether India and the United States will eventually conclude their trade agreement, but why a country aspiring to become a leading global power should allow the uncertainties of any single bilateral relationship to determine so much of its economic and diplomatic room for manoeuvre?

What if the real measure of strategic autonomy is not how emphatically New Delhi declares its independence, but how many credible alternatives it possesses when Washington imposes conditions, Beijing restricts opportunities, energy markets become unstable and negotiations reach an impasse?

And what if the most important shift in Indian foreign policy is not a dramatic realignment away from the United States, but a quieter redistribution of diplomatic attention towards countries that may individually possess less power than Washington or Beijing, yet collectively offer India something indispensable: the ability to negotiate without being trapped by dependence?

Your Worldview commentary presents a question that deserves to be examined far beyond the immediate tariff dispute:

Has India devoted so much strategic attention to the world's most powerful countries that it has undervalued the cumulative economic, technological and diplomatic power of everyone else?

That question becomes especially significant because you do not examine the India–US relationship merely through summit photographs, defence agreements or declarations of strategic convergence.

You examine what happens when the relationship is tested where political goodwill meets economic interests: immigration, investment, market access, energy security, technology regulation, sanctions and the domestic political calculations of both countries.

The underlying argument is more sophisticated than a call to replace one partner with another.

It asks whether India has sufficiently developed a foreign policy capable of preserving cooperation with major powers without becoming excessively vulnerable to their unilateral decisions.

And that is a question Suhasini Haidar has explored repeatedly in her reporting and analysis of strategic autonomy, great-power competition, the Global South and India's relationships beyond Washington and Beijing.

Written by Dolly Parton and immortalized by Whitney Houston, the song demands extraordinary control, breath support, and emotional truth. Alyona doesn’t imitate. She inhabits it: clear, free, intimate, and technically fearless. Listeners describe goosebumps, tears, and the sense that Whitney would have been honored. She handles the soaring peaks with strength and the quieter lines with genuine tenderness.

On YouTube, find Aly at https://t.co/XvlkP07tdZ… the cover has approached a million views. Her channel (roughly 412K subscribers, more than a thousand covers) is a living archive of classic rock, power ballads, and pop. Every video is fully self-produced in her home studio — arrangement, piano, vocals, mixing, mastering, filming, and editing. That hands-on process creates a direct, unfiltered intimacy you rarely get from label productions. Yet YouTube’s copyright system often blocks meaningful earnings on covers, turning viral discovery into a bittersweet gift: massive reach without sustainable income. The platform gives the song wings; it does not always feed the artist.

World Porridge Day🥣🌾🥣♨️🥛🥣🍚🥄🥛😋

World Porridge Day, observed annually on October 10, raises awareness and funds to help provide nutritious meals to children facing hunger. The day is organized by the Scottish charity Mary’s Meals, which serves children in Malawi, Zambia, and Zimbabwe steaming mugs of vitamin-enriched porridge. Its school-feeding programs provide one meal each school day, helping children attend class and learn.

Most people think of oatmeal when they think of porridge. However, there are other types of starchy plants that are used for porridge. These include rice, wheat, barley, corn, and buckwheat. Some porridge lovers add milk to their porridge, while others are content with just water. Fresh fruit, especially blueberries or bananas, adds a sweet touch. Other tasty additions to porridge include honey, peanut butter, nuts, raisins, baked apples and cinnamon, and even chocolate.

People who eat porridge regularly enjoy many health benefits. Besides improving heart health, porridge made with whole grains provides a boost to bone mineral density and reduces the risk of diabetes. Eating porridge can even increase life expectancy. It’s also a great meal as it helps you feel full longer.

Along with the deliciousness and the health benefits of porridge, it’s also inexpensive to make. 

Learn the Health Benefits of Oats and Porridge

Porridge can be a very healthy and beneficial meal for the body. It’s especially great to eat in the morning, as the body has lost a significant amount of nutrients overnight. Porridge helps to replenish them.

Studies have shown that a regular diet that includes porridge offers a variety of health benefits to humans, such as:

Rich in fiber
Many adults don’t have enough fiber in their diets today so porridge is a great way to add fiber that is vital to keeping the digestive system flowing.

Vitamins and Minerals
Vitamins E and B, zinc, copper, manganese, magnesium, folate and iron are all included in porridge, making it healthful for adults and children alike.

Energy Release
The high fiber in oat porridge slows the release of energy, helping the body to absorb the sugar instead of storing it away as fat.

Antioxidant Rich
Whole oats are high in polyphenols and antioxidants, which can help to clean out the cells, lower the blood pressure and reduce inflammation.

text:
Whenever I see Quran 4:157 cited as a mic-drop argument, I marvel at the intellectual audacity. 

The verse makes one of the most consequential historical claims in religious debate, yet offers no developed argument for it. 

When biblical figures challenged established beliefs, they did not merely announce that the other side was wrong. They entered the shared scriptural record, interrogated its language, exposed assumptions, and reasoned from premises their opponents could recognise.

In Romans 4, for instance, Paul argues that righteousness comes through faith rather than works of the Law. He does not announce a new revelation that cancels the existing record. He returns to Genesis 15:6, where Abraham’s faith is “credited to him as righteousness”, noting that if righteousness were earned, it would be a wage owed rather than a gift of grace. 

Then he delivers the decisive chronological point: was Abraham justified before or after circumcision? 

Genesis places the declaration of righteousness before circumcision. Circumcision therefore cannot be the prerequisite for what preceded it; it is merely a sign. Paul argues strictly from the text, through its vocabulary and chronology, to his conclusion.

Jesus demonstrates the same discipline. When the Sadducees deny the resurrection, he directs them to Exodus 3, where God identifies himself as the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, drawing an argument about the living God and the resurrection. 

When challenging assumptions about the Messiah, he invokes Psalm 110 and asks how David can call the Messiah Lord if the Messiah is merely David’s son. 

Whether one agrees with every interpretive move is beside the point. These are arguments. The reasoning is exposed for the audience to examine.

Now compare that with Quran 4:157. The crucifixion is the foundation of the New Testament and the most secure historical fact of Jesus’s life. Yet the Quran dismisses that entire event in half a verse: they neither killed him nor crucified him, but it was made to appear so to them. There is no textual exegesis, no engagement with the prophetic record, and no alternative historical narrative.

If we read this through the classical substitution view, the theological problem only worsens. 

God causing another person to look like Jesus means God deliberately manufactured the visual evidence that launched the Christian faith. It means God staged an illusion, allowed generations to die for proclaiming what they faithfully witnessed, and then faulted people centuries later for falling for it.

It will not do to plead that close scriptural debate was simply outside the Quran’s style. The verse is directed at communities that spent centuries testing theological claims with extreme rigor. 

Early Christians and Second Temple Jews were notoriously stubborn, scripturally literate disputants who demanded receipts at every turn. They produced texts like Hebrews, steeped in intricate legal and typological forensics, and they willingly went to Roman arenas over the historical reality of the cross. To imagine that an audience with that intellectual pedigree could ever be answered by an isolated, unargued sentence borders on absurd.

That is why celebrating that the Quran is clear completely misses the point. Clarity is easy, justification is hard. A bare assertion six centuries removed cannot dismantle the historical record simply because it speaks with confidence.

text:
The Widow’s Two Coins — She Gave All She Had | Mark 12:41–44
What made a poor widow’s two small coins more remarkable than the large offerings of wealthy people? In this powerful Bible story, Jesus reveals that God looks beyond the size of a gift to the heart and sincerity behind it.

In Mark 12:41–44, Jesus watched people giving at the temple treasury. While many gave large amounts, a poor widow offered two small copper coins. Though her gift appeared insignificant to others, Jesus used her example to teach His disciples a profound lesson about sacrifice, devotion, and generosity.

This message reminds us that our value before God is not determined by wealth, recognition, or the size of our achievements. We can honor God through our kindness, prayers, service, time, talents, and resources.

True generosity comes from a willing heart, guided by wisdom and love—not pressure or the desire to impress others.

Key lessons from the widow’s offering:

God sees the heart behind every act of giving.
Never despise small acts of kindness and service.
Be faithful with the gifts and opportunities God has given you.
Serve God without seeking human recognition.
Give willingly, wisely, and with genuine love.
📖 Scripture: Mark 12:41–44

🙏 Prayer: Heavenly Father, give us generous hearts and sincere motives. Teach us to use our time, talents, and resources to serve You and bless others. Help us remain faithful in little things and honor You in everything we do. In Jesus’ mighty name, Amen.

🇺🇸 🚨 FLORIDA DEPARTMENT OF EDUCATION: 4.8M STUDENT RECORDS ALLEGEDLY OFFERED FOR SALE

A threat actor on an underground forum claims to be selling a dataset of about 4.8 million student records allegedly taken from the Florida Department of Education (FLDOE).

The actor claims the dataset includes:
* Social Security numbers
* Full names, dates of birth and gender codes
* Street addresses, email addresses and phone numbers

According to the listing, the records cover financial-aid applicants over roughly 20 years, with birth years from the 1960s to 2009.

⚠️ Analyst Note:
If genuine, SSNs tied to dates of birth create long-term identity-theft risk, and many of those affected would have been minors when they applied, which makes their credit files attractive targets for fraud. FLDOE had not confirmed an incident at the time of writing.

This is an unverified threat-actor claim, NOT confirmation that FLDOE was breached.
